hi,

before installing ggplot2, try:

install_github("scales")

and maybe (probably not need to do) you need to resolve dependencies.
perhaps other packages than scales and ggplot2 are already on CRAN.

messages.subject: Re: install_github("ggplot2",branch="develop") -- package ‘scales’ is not available (for R version 2.13.1)
parts:
I was able to install_github("scales") but only if dev_mode(on=FALSE)
So the incantation from a completely fresh 2.13.1 was...

install.packages("devtools")
library(devtools)
install_github("scales")
dev_mode()
install_github("ggplot2",branch="develop")

but surely it is an error that install_github("scales") cannot resolve the dependencies when dev_mode(on=TRUE)?

This fails...

> library(devtools)
> dev_mode()

messages.subject: Re: install_github("ggplot2",branch="develop") -- package ‘scales’ is not available (for R version 2.13.1)
parts:
Hi,

probably this is problem of install.packages in windows.

install_github finally calls install.packages with type="source", so
probably the problem occurs in the install.packages in windows.
install.package with type="source" internally calls R CMD INSTALL as
shell command, and, in windows, the path-to-library is set via system
environment variable, i.e., Sys.setenv.

So, it may be helpful:

1. debug(install.package)
2. call install_github
3. in debug mode, run just before shell command: the line, if (system(cmd) > 0L)
4. inspect the cmd
5. inspect the system environment variable by Sys.getenv()

if these works,

Sys.setenv(HOGE="hoge")
Sys.getenv("HOGE")
system("set") # In my memory, "set" is windows counterpart of bash
"export." anyway, call the command showing environment variables.

and inspect the output. It should contain something like HOGE=hoge.

Probably I can test these in a few days.

--

The University of  Tokyo, Japan.

messages.subject: Re: install_github("ggplot2",branch="develop") -- package ‘scales’ is not available (for R version 2.13.1)
parts:
I found that install.packages(type=source) is not called in this case.  
Instead it uses devtools::build where it tries to run R CMD build.
I have no R startup files so build has no clue that dependency packages have been installed in a non-standard place.
The R_LIBS environment variable is not set.
As a quick hack, Sys.setenv(R_LIBS=.filePaths()[1]) before the R(cmd,path) worked. 
 
> build
function (pkg = NULL, path = NULL, binary = FALSE) 
{
    pkg <- as.package(pkg)
    if (is.null(path)) {
        path <- dirname(pkg$path)
    }
    if (binary) {
        cmd <- paste("CMD INSTALL ", shQuote(pkg$path), " --build", 
            sep = "")
        ext <- if (os() == "win") 
            "zip"
        else "tgz"
    }
    else {
        cmd <- paste("CMD build ", shQuote(pkg$path), " --no-manual --no-vignettes", 
            sep = "")
        ext <- "tar.gz"
    }
    R(cmd, path)
    targz <- paste(pkg$package, "_", pkg$version, ".", ext, sep = "")
    file.path(path, targz)
}
<environment: namespace:devtools>

In install.packages the R_LIBS are setup up like this to take into account the different platforms,
so I guess something similar needs to take place in devtools::build as well.

    libpath <- .libPaths()
    libpath <- libpath[!libpath %in% .Library]
    if (length(libpath)) 
        libpath <- paste(libpath, collapse = .Platform$path.sep)
    cmd0 <- paste(file.path(R.home("bin"), "R"), "CMD INSTALL")
    if (length(libpath)) 
        if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") {
            oldrlibs <- Sys.getenv("R_LIBS")
            Sys.setenv(R_LIBS = libpath)
            on.exit(Sys.setenv(R_LIBS = oldrlibs))
        }
        else cmd0 <- paste(paste("R_LIBS", shQuote(libpath), 
            sep = "="), cmd0)

> On Thu, Aug 11, 2011 at 8:02 AM, peta <pwh...@bhvr.com> wrote:
>> I found that install.packages(type=source) is not called in this case.
>> Instead it uses devtools::build where it tries to run R CMD build.
>> I have no R startup files so build has no clue that dependency packages have
>> been installed in a non-standard place.
>> The R_LIBS environment variable is not set.
>> As a quick hack, Sys.setenv(R_LIBS=.filePaths()[1]) before the R(cmd,path)
>> worked.
>>
>>> build
>> function (pkg = NULL, path = NULL, binary = FALSE)
>> {
>>     pkg <- as.package(pkg)
>>     if (is.null(path)) {
>>         path <- dirname(pkg$path)
>>     }
>>     if (binary) {
>>         cmd <- paste("CMD INSTALL ", shQuote(pkg$path), " --build",
>>             sep = "")
>>         ext <- if (os() == "win")
>>             "zip"
>>         else "tgz"
>>     }
>>     else {
>>         cmd <- paste("CMD build ", shQuote(pkg$path), " --no-manual
>> --no-vignettes",
>>             sep = "")
>>         ext <- "tar.gz"
>>     }
>>     R(cmd, path)
>>     targz <- paste(pkg$package, "_", pkg$version, ".", ext, sep = "")
>>     file.path(path, targz)
>> }
>> <environment: namespace:devtools>
>> In install.packages the R_LIBS are setup up like this to take into account
>> the different platforms,
>> so I guess something similar needs to take place in devtools::build as well.
>>
>>     libpath <- .libPaths()
>>     libpath <- libpath[!libpath %in% .Library]
>>     if (length(libpath))
>>         libpath <- paste(libpath, collapse = .Platform$path.sep)
>>     cmd0 <- paste(file.path(R.home("bin"), "R"), "CMD INSTALL")
>>     if (length(libpath))
>>         if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") {
>>             oldrlibs <- Sys.getenv("R_LIBS")
>>             Sys.setenv(R_LIBS = libpath)
>>             on.exit(Sys.setenv(R_LIBS = oldrlibs))
>>         }
>>         else cmd0 <- paste(paste("R_LIBS", shQuote(libpath),
>>             sep = "="), cmd0)
>>

R CMD needs a --r-lib option.
